緩.meaning: At closing time, the arcade's tired <part>claw machine</part> finally lets its grip go floppy and drops every toy it was clutching, a loose <part>thread</part> from a teddy dangling out of the chute. The owner hangs a sign on the glass: 'Claw on break.' Even machines need to <kanji>slacken</kanji>.
緩.on: The owner tapes a pink <sound>car</sound>nation to the glass as a get-well card.
緩.kun: A <sound>yu</sound>zu rolls out of the chute, chased by a toy <sound>roo</sound>k.

慢.meaning: A cat lounges in a <part>hammock</part> on the porch, her <part>heartbeat</part> barely ticking, and sneers at every jogger huffing past. 'Why run,' she yawns, 'when you can sway?' Her lazy smirk is pure <kanji>ridicule</kanji>.
慢.on: A <sound>mon</sound>key in the tree above copies her yawn and smirks too.

昇.meaning: The rooster oversleeps, so the farmer hoists the <part>sun</part> into the sky himself, in a wooden <part>measuring box</part> on a pulley, one notch at a time. Each tug, the yard gets brighter. The rooster wakes and pretends he did it. Somehow the sun has to <kanji>rise up</kanji>.
昇.on: The farmer charges the neighbours a coin each to watch the <sound>show</sound>.
昇.kun: '<sound>No</sound>t bad,' says the rooster, and climbs a milk <sound>bo</sound>ttle to crow.

泣.meaning: A violinist sets her music on a <part>stand</part> and plays a song so sad that <part>water drops</part> roll down the stand, the walls and every cheek in the hall. Even the cello seems to sob. The whole audience starts to <kanji>cry</kanji>.
泣.on: In the bar next door, a man stops his game and sobs into his pool <sound>cue</sound>.
泣.kun: A man in the front row dries his eyes on a piece of <sound>na</sound>an.

透.meaning: A window cleaner wants to <part>excel</part> at his job, so he polishes the skate park's glass <part>ramp</part> until it seems to vanish. Skaters zoom up what looks like thin air, and pigeons bonk into it. It is perfectly <kanji>transparent</kanji>.
透.on: One skater stubs her big <sound>toe</sound> on it, since she can't see where it starts.
透.kun: At lunch he shines his box of <sound>su</sound>shi until you can see right through the lid.

排.meaning: A pirate's parrot is served a <part>fishbone</part> for dinner. It squawks, refuses the thing, and ties it to the ship's <part>anchor</part> before shoving both overboard, so it can never come back. That parrot will <kanji>repudiate</kanji> anything that isn't a cracker.
排.on: Then it demands honey straight from a buzzing <sound>hi</sound>ve.

牧.meaning: In a heatwave, a cowgirl walks her herd with a giant folding <part>fan</part>, cooling every <part>cow</part> in turn and singing it a lullaby. The herd grows so content that calves arrive by the dozen. She knows how to <kanji>breed</kanji> happy cattle.
牧.on: Her <sound>box</sound>er dog trots behind, gently herding the calves.
牧.kun: Each calf's <sound>ma</sound>ma grazes by a <sound>ki</sound>wi vine in the open field: a pasture.

悔.meaning: A dragon's <part>heartbeat</part> skips at 3 a.m. as he remembers sneezing fire on his own birthday cake: the candles, the scorched icing, the guests' singed eyebrows. <part>Every</part> night, the same pang of <kanji>regret</kanji>.
悔.on: To cheer himself up, he flies a <sound>ki</sound>te shaped like a cake.
悔.kun: He sends a sorry note to the <sound>coo</sound>k who baked it.

覧.meaning: At the palace pool, a royal <part>servant</part> stands on the <part>diving board</part> with a <part>camera</part>, snapping <part>two</part> photos of every swimmer, while a lifeguard chalks a <part>slash</part> beside each name. Later the queen reads the whole album, page by page, in slow <kanji>perusal</kanji>.
覧.on: Then she parades the album down the palace <sound>run</sound>way for the court to see.
覧.kun: A <sound>mee</sound>rkat peers over her shoulder to look too.

般.meaning: A <part>maiden</part> runs a ferry: her little <part>boat</part> takes a goat, a piano and a wedding cake across the lake in one trip, and she curtseys at every stop. Nothing is too big or too odd for her. She's the lake's best <kanji>carrier</kanji>.
般.on: Her fare is one pot of <sound>hon</sound>ey per passenger.

梅.meaning: A grumpy grandpa sits under his <part>tree</part> and counts the fruit. <part>Every</part> morning one is missing, and a purple-faced badger waddles past, whistling. Grandpa sighs and hands him another. It's the badger's favourite: a juicy <kanji>plum</kanji>.
梅.on: The badger rides off on a squeaky <sound>bi</sound>ke with the fruit in its basket.
梅.kun: Next day he swaps one for a bowl of <sound>u</sound>don and a slice of <sound>me</sound>lon.

操.meaning: A crane driver hooks an <part>anchor</part> under a kids' <part>treehouse</part> and swings it over three gardens, past washing lines and a startled cat, then lowers it gently into the new oak. The neighbours clap. That's a tricky <kanji>maneuver</kanji>.
操.on: The kids inside blow <sound>soa</sound>p bubbles the whole way over.
操.kun: A <sound>mee</sound>rkat in a <sound>sa</sound>ri guards the new treehouse with her pet <sound>o</sound>tter and never leaves its side: loyalty.

績.meaning: A palace seamstress always got the <part>blame</part> for every rip in the royal robes. So she stitches a tapestry of her best repairs in gold <part>thread</part>: patched capes, mended crowns, a dragon sewn back together. The king hangs it in the hall. It shows all her <kanji>exploits</kanji>.
績.on: Each <sound>sec</sound>tor of the tapestry shows a different year of her work.

剤.meaning: A pharmacist climbs a tall <part>ladder</part> to reach a giant's pill, big as a boulder, and saws off one slice with a <part>dagger</part>. 'Too much,' she mutters, and shaves off a crumb. A mouse with a cold swallows it. Just the right <kanji>dose</kanji>.
剤.on: Cured, the mouse plays a happy tune on a tiny <sound>xy</sound>lophone.
剤.kun: With a <sound>ca</sound>lm hand she snips a loose feather off a <sound>roo</sound>k waiting in line: to trim.

恩.meaning: A grumpy giant who scares everyone quietly fixes the village bridge every night, and won't say what the <part>cause</part> is. One morning the children catch him at it and bake him a pie shaped like a <part>heart</part>. He blushes bright red. Kindness kept secret like his is true <kanji>grace</kanji>.
恩.on: He's so flustered he flicks every <sound>on</sound> switch in the bakery.

刈.meaning: At harvest, the scarecrow is fed up with standing still. He grabs <part>scissors</part> in one hand and a <part>dagger</part> in the other and races through the wheat, snip-snip-slash, stacking sheaves behind him. The farmer wakes to a bare field. The scarecrow loves to <kanji>reap</kanji>.
刈.on: A <sound>gui</sound>de dog leads him back to his post before the crows notice.
刈.kun: Then he stands <sound>ca</sound>lm in the stubble, as if nothing happened.

稲.meaning: In <part>old times</part>, a heron got bored of fish and pushed one <part>claw</part> into the mud, planting a single <part>grain</part>. It sprouted, so she planted more. Now the whole wet valley waves green and her great-grandchildren wade through it. It all began with one <kanji>rice plant</kanji>.
稲.on: She still checks each new sprout by poking it with her <sound>toe</sound>.
稲.kun: An <sound>ee</sound>l slips between the stalks, dodging a farmer's <sound>ne</sound>t.

彫.meaning: A sculptor works with a cat curled on his <part>lap</part>, and to pass the time he chisels its portrait into a pumpkin. He gets the ears right, then spends an hour on the <part>whiskers</part>, one fine groove each. The cat yawns and leaves. He's still there, learning to <kanji>carve</kanji>.
彫.on: He finishes the pumpkin cat with a tiny <sound>cho</sound>ker etched round its neck.
彫.kun: Next he chisels a <sound>ho</sound>tdog out of a carrot for lunch.

隠.meaning: At the village fair, a shy dragon has a crush on the baker. She holds up a <part>pennant</part> to hide her face, tucks one <part>claw</part> behind a garden <part>rake</part>, and presses her glowing <part>heart</part> flat against the hay. The baker walks right past. She has a lot to <kanji>conceal</kanji>.
隠.on: She writes him a love note in invisible <sound>in</sound>k.
隠.kun: She slips the note into his <sound>ca</sound>rt, then hides behind the <sound>coo</sound>k.

貫.meaning: A woodpecker mistakes a giant clam for a tree. Tap, tap, tap: it drills a neat round <part>window</part> straight through the <part>shellfish</part>, and the clam peers out, rather pleased with the view. That beak can <kanji>pierce</kanji> anything.
貫.on: The clam hangs a pink <sound>car</sound>nation in its new window.
貫.kun: A <sound>tsu</sound>nami rolls in, the crowd on the beach shouts '<sound>Rah</sound>!', and the woodpecker hides in a <sound>noo</sound>k.

尾.meaning: A dog wants to join the parade but has nothing to wave, so he ties a <part>flag</part> to his back end. It falls off. He glues on a ball of <part>fur</part> from the hairbrush instead; that falls off too. In the end he just wags. The best thing to wave is a <kanji>tail</kanji>.
尾.on: A <sound>bee</sound>tle rides on the wagging tip all the way to the end of the parade.
尾.kun: '<sound>Oh</sound>!' gasps the crowd, as one big wag knocks over the drummer.

漢.meaning: A <part>husband</part> paddles a canoe east for a whole year, flicking <part>water drops</part> off his paddle and cooking <part>grass</part> soup when the snacks run out. When he finally lands, he opens his <part>mouth</part> and reads hello from his notebook of brush-drawn characters. He has reached <kanji>China</kanji>.
漢.on: On the beach, a smiling stranger hands him a pink <sound>car</sound>nation.

剣.meaning: At a <part>campsite</part>, a scout leader toasts marshmallows on a little <part>dagger</part>, but they keep falling in the fire. So he forges a longer blade, then longer still, until he's waving one as tall as the tent. Now his marshmallows hang from a <kanji>sabre</kanji>.
剣.on: His dog watches from her <sound>ken</sound>nel, waiting for one to drop.
剣.kun: A sudden <sound>tsu</sound>nami of rain hits, so he shoos a <sound>roo</sound>k and two <sound>gee</sound>se into the tent.

筒.meaning: A postman cuts <part>bamboo</part> stalks into tubes all the <part>same</part> size, slips a letter inside each one and rolls them down the hills to every farm. One rolls into a pond and floats off like a boat. Each letter travels in its own <kanji>cylinder</kanji>.
筒.on: One rolls straight over a farmer's big <sound>toe</sound>.
筒.kun: '<sound>Tsu</sound>! <sound>Tsu</sound>!' the farmer hisses through his teeth, hopping on one foot.

択.meaning: A sailor shopping for a new <part>anchor</part> lays them all out on the dock and takes the <part>measure</part> of each with a tape: too small, too rusty, too shaped like a duck. In the end she picks the duck one. It was hard to <kanji>choose</kanji>.
択.on: She celebrates with a crunchy <sound>ta</sound>co on the dock.
択.kun: The shopkeeper throws in a free <sound>e</sound>gg and shouts '<sound>Rah</sound>!' as she sails off.

棄.meaning: Moving house, a man fills a crate with junk: an old pot <part>lid</part>, a shirt with a hole at the <part>elbow</part>, a <part>comb</part> with no teeth. He leaves it under a <part>tree</part> with a sign saying 'Free!' Nobody takes a thing, not even the squirrels. Some things you just have to <kanji>abandon</kanji>.
棄.on: On top of the pile he leaves the old house <sound>key</sound>.
棄.kun: A stray cat sniffs the crate and drags off a <sound>su</sound>shi roll from the bin beside it.

柔.meaning: A whaler retires and hangs his old <part>harpoon</part> on the apple <part>tree</part> in his garden. Moss grows on it, sparrows nest in it, and the apples below are bruised by nothing harsher than rain. Now he spends his days feeding ducks, as <kanji>tender</kanji> as a ripe peach.
柔.on: He keeps his old medal, a sea-green <sound>jew</sound>el, in the sparrows' nest.
柔.kun: He hums to the baby in the next <sound>ya</sound>rd until it stops its '<sound>wah</sound>' and smiles.

勧.meaning: A timid <part>sparrow</part> perches at the end of a <part>diving board</part>, too scared to fly. A coach flexes a <part>muscle</part>, points a <part>dart</part> at the water and draws a <part>slash</part> in the air: 'Go!' After an hour of pep talk, she leaps and soars. It took a lot to <kanji>persuade</kanji> her.
勧.on: The crowd throws a pink <sound>car</sound>nation into the pool for her.
勧.kun: The coach treats her to <sound>su</sound>shi and a brush to clean the <sound>soo</sound>t off her wings.

旗.meaning: A librarian sails across the lake on a raft made from a <part>bookshelf</part>, with a bedsheet <part>sail</part> and a <part>diving board</part> nailed on the front. At the top of the mast she hoists a hanky painted with a shushing finger. Every boat goes quiet under her <kanji>flag</kanji>.
旗.on: Below it hangs the <sound>key</sound> to the library, jingling in the wind.
旗.kun: A <sound>ha</sound>rp seal pops up to borrow a book, nibbling a <sound>ta</sound>co.

壁.meaning: A chili seller is tired of customers sneezing on her peppers, so she piles <part>soil</part> around her <part>chili stall</part>, higher and higher, packing it hard. Soon only her sign peeks over the top, and the sneezing stops. She has built a <kanji>wall</kanji>.
壁.on: She pats each clod of soil into a neat <sound>hex</sound>agon before stacking it.
壁.kun: Behind it she naps, <sound>ca</sound>lm as a cat, in a <sound>be</sound>d of red peppers.
